name: Progressive Polyneuropathy with Bilateral Striatal Necrosis
aliases: Progressive Peripheral Neuropathy and Striatal Degeneration

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Progressive Polyneuropathy with Bilateral Striatal Necrosis

criteria.description: Progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy with distal weakness and sensory loss
Bilateral striatal necrosis demonstrated by MRI or CT imaging
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal and demyelinating polyneuropathy
Exclusion of other metabolic, infectious, or toxic causes of polyneuropathy and basal ganglia lesions
Positive family history consistent with inherited neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy plus bilateral striatal necrosis on imaging, supported by electrophysiological findings and exclusion of other causes.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist in confirming diagnosis if causative mutations are identified.

searchTerms: brain imaging showing striatal tissue death
bilateral basal ganglia damage on MRI
worsening numbness and weakness in hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Extrapyramidal movement disorders including dystonia and chorea
searchTerms: involuntary movements like twisting and jerking
movement disorders with dystonia and chorea

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness predominantly in distal limbs
Sensory loss including vibration and proprioception deficits
searchTerms: loss of vibration and position sense

common.symptomName: Gait disturbance due to neuropathy and extrapyramidal symptoms
searchTerms: walking difficulties from nerve and movement issues
gait problems due to neuropathy and movement disorder
unsteady walking from nerve and extrapyramidal symptoms

common.symptomName: Hyporeflexia or areflexia in affected limbs
Mild cognitive impairment or executive dysfunction

occasional.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction such as orthostatic hypotension
searchTerms: autonomic nervous system problems causing low blood pressure

rare.symptomName: Seizures secondary to basal ganglia involvement
searchTerms: seizures caused by basal ganglia damage
epileptic episodes from deep brain involvement
brain seizures linked to movement center

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations including depression or psychosis
Respiratory muscle weakness leading to respiratory insufficiency
searchTerms: weak breathing muscles causing breathing failure
respiratory muscle weakness leading to insufficiency

laboratory: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein without pleocytosis
Normal routine blood tests excluding metabolic causes
imaging: MRI showing bilateral symmetrical necrosis of the striatum (caudate and putamen)
T2 hyperintensity and volume loss in basal ganglia
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with mitochondrial or metabolic disorders causing striatal necrosis (if identified)
other: Electromyography demonstrating mixed axonal and demyelinating polyneuropathy
Nerve biopsy may show axonal degeneration

distinguishingFeatures: Family history with spastic paraplegia phenotype

redFlags: Rapid progression of neurological deficits over weeks to months
Onset of extrapyramidal symptoms with polyneuropathy
Bilateral basal ganglia lesions on imaging without alternative explanation
